\section[\texorpdfstring{\te{సేకరించు} (sēkariñcu)}{సేకరించు (sēkariñcu)}]{\te{సేకరించు} (sēkariñcu) — to collect}

\label{lesson:TE-C245-sekarincu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for to wilt, then the Telugu for to bark.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{సేకరించు}}
\textbf{\te{సేకరించు}} — \emph{sēkariñcu} — \textquotedblleft{}to collect\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
DEDR 2801 lists \textbf{\te{సేకరించు}} (\emph{sēkariñcu}), \textquotedblleft{}to save, collect\textquotedblright{}, with Tamil \emph{cēkaram}, \textquotedblleft{}acquisition, collection\textquotedblright{}, and notes that the Malayalam forms look Sanskrit though Sanskrit has no such word in this sense.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\te{ప్రసారం} \te{చేయు}} (\emph{prasāraṁ cēyu}) pairs Sanskrit \emph{prasāra}, \textquotedblleft{}extension, spreading\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 8835), with the Telugu ending \emph{-ṁ}, and native \emph{cēyu}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 1957).

\section[\texorpdfstring{\te{ముద్రించు} (mudriñcu)}{ముద్రించు (mudriñcu)}]{\te{ముద్రించు} (mudriñcu) — to print}

\label{lesson:TE-C245-mudrincu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for to collect, then the Telugu for to broadcast.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{ముద్రించు}}
\textbf{\te{ముద్రించు}} — \emph{mudriñcu} — \textquotedblleft{}to print\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\te{ముద్రించు}} (\emph{mudriñcu}) is Sanskrit \emph{mudrā}, \textquotedblleft{}seal, signet-ring\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10203), made into a verb with the Telugu ending \emph{-iñcu}: \textquotedblleft{}to stamp, print\textquotedblright{}. CDIAL thinks \emph{mudrā} probably came from Iranian.
\end{cousinweb}
